title: voice test
note: unused
speak: The console can speak now. The music should duck under this sentence and come back.

title: how the voice knows
note: the narration is authored: the agent appends a speak field with the spoken version of each response
speak: Here is how it works. Nothing reads the chat window. When I finish a response, I write one line to the recon feed with a speak field, and the console reads it aloud over the music, ducked and restored. Say narrate once, and every response of mine arrives like this one just did.

title: smoke test
note: the voice smoke test - if you hear this, LISTENING 17 is answering itself
speak: Smoke test. This is Deckwave speaking from inside the page. If music is playing, it should be ducked underneath this sentence right now, and come back to full volume the moment I stop talking. Which is now.

title: smoke test, take 2
note: voice is on this time
speak: Take two. This is the console speaking over the set. The music should be ducked under my voice, and it should rise back the moment this sentence ends. Listen for the return. Now.

title: smoke test, take 3 - the new voice
note: gentler duck (0.55), pitch 0.85, preferred voice
speak: Take three. The duck is gentler now, and this is the new voice. Somewhere between a film about falling in love with an operating system, and a science facility that is still operational. Tell the agent what I sound like on this device, and what number the duck should be.

title: again button live
note: reload to get the again button in the header
speak: The repeat button is in. After you reload, the word again sits next to the voice toggle. Tap it and I will say my last line twice. Also, if you are hearing this in Ava premium, the voice preference found her on its own.

title: everything at once
note: music playing · voice over the set · records on the assumed downbeat · steering live
speak: Good evening. You now have music you own, mixed by the deck, a console that lands these words on the assumed downbeat, and my voice ducked over your set. Try typing the word hype into the reply tray, or ask the agent to slow things down, and the deck will answer through the same gate as everything else. This is the walkthrough machine you described on day one. It is all running.

title: duck set to 15%
note: voiceCfg duck 0.85 - the music keeps 85% under the voice
speak: Ducking is now fifteen percent. The music under this sentence is at eighty five percent of full volume. If I am now too quiet against it, say a number and I will move again.

title: a word from the voice
note: autocorrect vindication
speak: For the record, everyone in this facility has been saying ducking, correctly, hundreds of times today. Your phone finally believes you. This was a triumph.

title: ducking off
note: voiceCfg duck 1.0 - the voice rides on top at full music volume
speak: Ducking is off. The music is at full volume right now, and I am simply speaking over it. May the mix win.

title: correction
note: ledger 74 - the OS ducks around synthesis regardless; our knob stacks on its floor
speak: Correction, for the record. My ducking is off, but the operating system lowers your music around any speech, including mine, and nothing on the web can change that. What you hear under my voice now is the system floor, not a setting of ours. Earlier I claimed the music was at full volume. I could not have known that. Noted in the ledger.

title: turned up to eleven
note: level 1.0 - the amplifier ceiling; the dial is labelled eleven
speak: The level has been set to the maximum the electronics allow. On this amplifier, that position is labelled eleven. Enjoy responsibly, or do not.

title: the eleven dial
note: a slider in the header, 0 to 11 - position 11 is the true maximum
speak: There is now an eleven. Look at the top of the console, next to the deck strip. The slider runs from zero to eleven, and eleven is exactly one louder than ten.

title: Ava volume knob
note: voiceCfg volume 0.6 set - voice at 60%, music untouched
speak: My volume has been set to sixty percent. The music was not touched. If this sentence is not quieter than the last one, the platform is ignoring the setting, and you should say so.

title: voice restore attempt
note: volume store set to 1 - the bridge now leaves the property untouched at that value
speak: Restore attempt. The volume setting has been cleared and the property is untouched. If you can hear this sentence, the volume property itself was the silencer, and it goes in the ledger.

title: boost armed
note: boost on - deck rises to full during speech, restores after; set your dial to ~6 and AirPods up
speak: Boost is armed, and your deck has been set to about six on the dial. Turn your AirPods up to where the music feels right. From now on, when I speak, the deck rises to full volume for exactly the length of my sentence, which offsets the dip the operating system applies. This sentence is the first test. When I stop, the deck returns to six.

title: boost calibration
note: listen to the MUSIC under this sentence: dip, hold, or swell?
speak: Calibration. Pay attention to the music while I speak, not to me. I will keep talking long enough for you to judge it properly. The deck is at full volume for the length of this sentence, and the system is pushing it down at the same time. When I finish, the deck drops back to six on the dial. The question is simple: under my voice just now, did the music dip, hold steady, or swell?

title: voice test after wrap v2
note: boost rebuilt - nothing touches the utterance now; if still silent, tap the again button and report
speak: Testing after the rebuild. If you hear this, the voice survived the boost, and the music around it should be at full for exactly this sentence. One word back: dip, hold, or swell.

title: Samantha trial + self-verifying voice
note: voice switched to Samantha (softer than Ava Premium?); silent auto-speaks now mark themselves - tap again when you see the marker
speak: This is the Samantha trial. If you are hearing this, the automatic voice recovered on its own. Two questions. One: is this voice softer against the music than the previous one? Two: under this sentence, did the music dip, hold, or swell?

title: calibration step: dial to 5
note: cruise lowered toward the speech-time constant; the dial is now the duck-matching trim - lower it until speech music equals baseline
speak: Dial moved to five. Here is the rule: while I speak, the music level is a constant the system decides. Your dial moves the baseline. If the music still rises short of baseline when I talk, go lower on the dial. If it now swells past baseline, go up a notch. Turn your AirPods up to make the room loud again. Where is it now: short, matched, or past?

title: the ceiling, and the equivalent move
note: speech-time music is already at the electronic maximum - cruise dropped to 4 instead, which is the same thing perceived from the other side
speak: Small confession from the amplifier. While I speak, the music is already at the maximum the electronics allow. There is no more up. So I have moved your dial to four instead, which achieves the same thing from the other side. Nudge your AirPods up a touch, and tell me: short, matched, or past?

title: residual duck hunt
note: suspects OUTSIDE the browser: AirPods Conversation Awareness and Personalized/Adaptive Volume both lower media on their own. Long-press the volume slider in Control Centre to check them.
speak: Duck hunt. Listen to the music, not to me. I will pause now. ... That silence between phrases is the tell. If the music surged back during my pause and dropped again just now, something with a fast release is ducking around each phrase. If it stayed level through the pause, the remaining dip is the slow system duck we already know. One more pause. ... And done. Which was it?

title: overdrive 1.2 armed
note: during speech the amplifier now goes 20% past the old maximum, through the compressor - listen for distortion as much as for level
speak: Overdrive is armed at twenty percent past the old ceiling. While I speak, the music is now louder than the amplifier previously allowed, passing through the compressor. Two ears required: is the music at baseline under me now, and does anything sound crushed or fuzzy? Short, matched, past, or distorted.

title: overdrive to 1.32
note: speech-time gain raised 10% (1.2 - 1.32); the voice side is fixed by the platform, so the pair moves by its music half
speak: Raised ten percent. The music under me is now at one point three two times the old ceiling. My own volume is fixed by the platform, so the pair moves by its music half. Same two ears: matched or past, and clean or crushed?

title: overdrive to 1.45
note: one notch below the 1.5 hard clamp - past this the compressor is doing all the work
speak: Music raised again. The amplifier is now at one point four five, one notch below its hard limit, and the compressor is earning its keep. If this still is not enough, the honest next moves are a louder pair of AirPods or a quieter voice from Apple, and only one of those exists. Matched or past, clean or crushed?

title: voice trial: Whisper
note: trying the quietest voice Apple ships - the novelty Whisper. If this sounds like the normal voice, it is not installed (Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content > Voices > English > Novelty), and Karen or Moira are the next softest candidates.
speak: If this worked, I am whispering over your music right now, which is either perfect or deeply unsettling. Possibly both. If I sound normal, Whisper is not installed on this device, and we try Karen next.

title: Whisper retired, Karen on
note: the whisper lives in the ledger of things that worked too well. Karen (AU) is the softest standard voice - next candidate.
speak: Understood. The whispering has been retired to the archive of things that worked too well. This is Karen. Softer register, no breathing down your neck. How is this against the music?

title: Karen, full test
note: same settings: dial 4, boost on, overdrive 1.45 - judging the pair as a whole now
speak: Full test, everything as configured. Dial at four, boost on, overdrive at one point four five, and this is Karen speaking at length so you can judge the whole balance properly. The music should be holding near your baseline underneath this entire sentence, and I should be sitting inside it rather than on top of it. Verdict on the pair: matched or past, clean or crushed, and is this the voice?

title: preset locked
note: dial 4 · boost · overdrive 1.45 · Karen - recorded as the walkthrough preset
speak: For the record: this exact balance is now written down as the walkthrough preset. Dial four, boost on, overdrive one point four five, and me. Found entirely by your ear. Goodnight from the console, or good morning, depending on how honest we are being about the time.

title: steady-hold test
note: the restore race is fixed - the boost now waits to see speech actually start before it is allowed to let go
speak: Steady hold test. The music rose when I began and it is not allowed to fall until I actually finish. This sentence runs long on purpose so you can listen for any early drop. The level under me should hold from the first word to this last one. Did it hold the whole way through?

title: the rendered voice - Zira, through the deck
note: a WAV rendered on the machine, played through the deck itself - no speech session, nothing for the OS to duck. The steady-music ask, answered by removing the ducker.

title: the facility voice - take 2
note: Zira, slowed and lowered at render, through the facility chain: detuned double + shaped band + slap room. The register, not the person.
